title: Lightweight evals & quick takeaways (scratchpad)
body:
Purpose
- Brain dump: lightweight, low-cost evaluation patterns we can run frequently on hosted and dedicated combos. Focus: cheap signal for regressions and quality drift rather than full eval suites.

High-level thesis
- Continuous, cheap evals (CEs) that run on a sample of traffic + synthetic probes catch most real regressions earlier than monthly expensive eval runs.
- These should be: small (<=2k examples), fast (walltime < 30m), diverse (few targeted slices), and measurable in tokens/cost.

Quick reading list (notes)
- "Calibration for Prompted Models" (arXiv 2025): cheap prompt families + temperature sweep produce robust rank-based metrics. Takeaway: prefer relative metrics (win-rate vs baseline) over absolute probability thresholds.
- "On-device Distillation for Monitorable Models" (NeurIPS 2025 workshop): distill tiny eval heads to run at edge; interesting for private deployments where we want local drift signals. Idea: deploy tiny comparator head that computes a 3-way quality score.
- "Sampling strategies for eval under budget constraints" (ICML 2026): stratified sampling by token-length and top-p distribution reduces variance of metric estimates. Practical: precompute slice weights by route and sample during traffic capture.

Practical patterns to try (ranked)
1) Rolling micro-suite (recommended first experiment)
   - 500 examples: 300 real user queries (sampled per-route), 200 synthetic probes (common edge cases). Run every 6 hours on dedicated pool spare capacity.
   - Metrics: relative win-rate vs last stable model (pairwise), avg edit distance for structured outputs, 95p latency.

2) Prompt-ladder A/B comparisons
   - For prompt / instruction changes, run short A/B (n=1000 each) with a concise rubric (1-3 quality buckets via heuristics) to catch regressions before rollout.

3) Streaming quality counters (cheap on-host logs)
   - Micro-signals computed in runtime: hallucination heuristics (assertion mismatch), token-fluency score (LM perplexity delta), structured-parse-success flag. Emit as metrics with short retention.

Lightweight probes: examples to include - factual lookups (short & long context) - numeric reasoning puzzle (simple arithmetic, date arithmetic) - format fidelity (JSON/table output) - safety edge (ambiguous instruction)

Metric suggestions (fast, interpretable)
- Pairwise win-rate (modelA vs modelB) via simple heuristics (BLEU-ish for structured outputs or normalized string match).
- Parse success rate for structured outputs (regex-based).
- Small-bert embed similarity for semantic drift (cheap 384-dim).
- Latency p95 and tail counts > X ms bucketed by route.

Implementation notes for Redwood constraints
- Hosted API: can run on low-priority tenant; use sampling hook in Console to export examples to eval pipeline. Need to ensure PII redaction before storing.
- Dedicated: use spare reserved capacity windows (off-peak) to run heavier micro-suites. Configure autoscale to allow short bursts.
- Private: push short eval harness that ships with the private agent; local telemetry to KMS-protected S3 equivalent.

Open questions / research notes
- How correlated are cheap pairwise win-rate metrics with human evals for long-form generation? We need an experiment comparing 2k cheap signals vs 200 human labels.
- Can we build a tiny learned comparator (binary classifier) trained on historical A/B human labels that generalizes across model sizes? Risk: overfitting to idiosyncratic labeler distributions.
- Sampling: should slice by route or by user? Route is easier (deterministic), user might capture behavioral drift but has privacy/PII concerns.

Experiment template (for infra/owner: Samir)
- Name: rolling-micro-6h-v1
- Sample: 300 route-sampled real examples (last 6h), cap per-route 50
- Synthetic probe set: curated 200 (store in repo)
- Models: current-stable vs candidate
- Metrics: pairwise win-rate, parse success, p95 latency, cost delta
- Run cadence: every 6h for 14 days, then review

Notes to self (TODOs)
- [ ] Make synthetic probe repo (start with 3 categories: factual, numeric, format)
- [ ] Add quick script to fetch sampled traffic via Admin API with PII filter
- [ ] Prototype small comparator model in eval-probes repo (PR link above)
- [ ] Get sign-off from privacy for storing 6h sampled traffic

Random ideas (brainstorm)
- Bandit-driven probe selection: allocate eval budget to probes that maximally reduce uncertainty in pairwise win-rate.
- Canary lightweight: route 0.1% of traffic through a light comparator that flags >5% regressions to interrupt rollout.
- Delta-cost alerting: not just latency regressions but token-cost-per-response drift vs baseline.

References / links (fast)
- arXiv:2601.01234 cheap eval ladders (see linked_artifacts)
- Internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-probes/pull/78
- Jira: INFR-412 (sampling hook)

Final quick next step (for this week)
- Draft the rolling-micro-6h-v1 runbook and share with Samir + Maya. Keep it intentionally small - goal is signal not exhaustive coverage.

Unresolved: what threshold should trigger rollback? Proposal: if pairwise win-rate drops by >6 percentage points with p<0.05 and parse success delta >3pp over two consecutive runs, auto-pause rollout and create alert. Need stats review.

End of scratchpad (will iteratively refine)
